subject: can we have 2 aes in on plot?

messages.author: 36ec1331d4d5918f
messages.subject: can we have 2 aes in on plot?
parts:
Hi,

I thought geom_text would allow me to place some annotations on a plot, but in my case, I have one annotation for each x value, but the y coordinate does not correspond to the data already plotted. I give two ways I've displayed sample size for each year of data collection on a plot showing an index of average fish stomach content volume for each year.

example 1: http://dl.dropbox.com/u/612902/EX1.pdf

example 2: http://dl.dropbox.com/u/612902/EX2.pdf

Is there a way to do this with ggplot2?

Thanks,

Denis

messages.author: 36ec1331d4d5918f
messages.subject: Re: can we have 2 aes in on plot?
parts:
Hi Ista,

easily done:

N <- c(462, 502, 928, 1678, 1195, 549, 1329, 1036, 683, 756, 602, 478, 337, 188, 464)
Fullness <- c(0.8093504, 0.3608854, 0.5566173, 0.4807727, 0.4665601, 0.5827983, 0.4037285,
0.4424525, 0.6676613, 0.5445564, 0.5818099, 0.3650190, 0.3451034, 0.2409323, 0.3187466)
Year <- c(1993, 1994, 1995, 1996, 1997, 1998, 1999, 2001, 2002, 2003, 2004, 2005, 2006, 2007, 2008)

#ex1:
par(mar=c(2.8, 2.8, 1.5, 0.2)+0.1, mgp=c(1.8,0.5,0),xpd=NA, cex.lab=1.2)
les.x= barplot(Fullness, names.arg=Year, col = gray(0.75), ylim=c(0,0.9),xlab="Year",
ylab="Total stomach fullness index")
mySeq=c(-0.3, les.x)
text(mySeq, par("usr")[4], c("N =", N), adj=c(0.5,-0.1), cex=0.7)

#ex2:
par(mar=c(2.8, 2.8, 1, 0.2)+0.1, mgp=c(1.8,0.5,0), cex.lab=1.2)
les.x= barplot(Fullness, names.arg=Year, col = gray(0.75), ylim=c(0,0.9),xlab="Year",
ylab="Total stomach fullness index")
height_in_col = par("usr")[3]
text(les.x, height_in_col, N, adj=c(-0.5,0.5),cex=0.9, srt=90)

messages.subject: Re: can we have 2 aes in on plot?
parts:
df1<-data.frame(N, Fullness, Year)
df1

ggplot(data=df1)+
geom_bar(aes(x=as.factor(Year), y=Fullness))+
geom_text(aes(x=as.factor(Year), y=0.005, label=N), hjust=0, angle=90, color="white")+
labs(x="Year", y="Toadal Stomach Fullness Index")+
theme_bw()

That's similar to your second example. Not sure how to do the first one so easily. 

B

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: can we have 2 aes in on plot?
parts:
The first one can be approximated as

df1<-data.frame(N, Fullness, Year)
ggplot(data=df1)+
geom_bar(aes(x=as.factor(Year), y=Fullness))+
geom_text(aes(x=as.factor(Year), y=0.9, label=N), size=3)+

annotate("text", x=0, y=.9, label="n = ", size=3) +
theme_bw()

Best,
Ista
